subject.title: Bound batch file read with size cap in config-set-input

question: Should `openclaw config set --batch-file` adopt a fixed 8 MiB hard rejection limit for existing batch inputs, and what compatibility behavior is intended for larger valid files?
rationale: The shared reader is an appropriate primitive, but the maximum size and fail-closed behavior are user-visible CLI compatibility policy rather than a mechanically derivable implementation detail.

options.title: Define and validate a supported limit
options.body: Choose and document a justified cap, then add direct CLI proof for normal, exact-limit, and oversized batch files before merge.

options.title: Accept the 8 MiB compatibility break
options.body: Land the current cutoff only with an explicit maintainer decision that existing larger batch inputs should fail with the new diagnostic.

options.title: Pause this narrow PR
options.body: Defer the cutoff until a shared policy for configuration-import input sizes is established.

recommendation.title: Define and validate a supported limit
recommendation.body: Choose and document a justified cap, then add direct CLI proof for normal, exact-limit, and oversized batch files before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the cited adjacent bounded-read pattern and can route the chosen compatibility contract into the focused patch.
